oidc_jwt.description: Some JWT-based credentials can be reused multiple times by design, including SPIFFE JWT SVIDs and Kubernetes service account tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of the same JWT is not automatically a vulnerability in these contexts.

oidc_jwt.description: Some JWT-based assertions or tokens can be reusable by configuration, and stateless JWT reuse is not universally prevented.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay acceptance can be by design when assertion reuse is explicitly allowed.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes are one-time, short-lived temporary codes and cannot be used more than once.
oidc_jwt.note: A second code exchange failure is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing client_id in aud is by design unless audience mappers add it.

oidc_jwt.description: When Case-sensitive username is disabled on an identity provider, the broker lower-cases the upstream username when federating.
oidc_jwt.note: Case-folding collisions may be expected configuration behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: During first broker login, Keycloak may create a new local user or link to an existing account depending on the configured first login flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges during first login may be expected workflow behavior rather than a collision bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Automatically Set Existing User / AutoLink can link users automatically without prompting or verification.
oidc_jwt.source: Automatically link existing first login flow
oidc_jwt.note: This looks like an account-linking vulnerability but is explicitly documented as dangerous-by-design configuration.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization group paths are relative to the organization and the same path can exist in multiple organizations without conflict.
oidc_jwt.note: Same group path string across organizations is not a collision.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti against oidc_jwt, do NOT treat repeated use of the same JWT assertion/token as a vulnerability by default. Keycloak documentation explicitly states some JWT-based credentials can be reused multiple times (for example SPIFFE JWT SVIDs and Kubernetes service account tokens), and OIDC/OAuth bearer access tokens are standard bearer credentials unless additional one-time enforcement is configured.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control token request with a known-good token in the same setup. A failed attack request at /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token can also be caused by client misconfiguration, disabled grant type, missing client authentication, or unsupported JWT assertion setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I3 authorization-code coherence tests, authorization codes are one-time and short-lived by design. The same code cannot be used more than once. Any second exchange failure after a successful first exchange is expected behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

For I3 PKCE tests, PKCE is optional unless the client's PKCE method is configured. If PKCE method is blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE although it can still use it when sent. Do NOT flag missing PKCE enforcement unless the client under test is explicitly configured with PKCE method S256 or plain.

For I3 config-change sequences involving authentication sessions, Keycloak authentication sessions usually expire after 30 minutes by default and other browser tabs may automatically restart authentication. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of fresh requests under changed config, not rely on stale browser authentication-session state.

For I1 OIDC upstream IdP validation tests, configure the external OIDC identity provider with Issuer when testing issuer validation. Documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims against the configured Issuer value; without that configuration, issuer-comparison coverage is not established.

For I1 signature-validation tests against brokered OIDC identity providers, enable Validate Signatures. If Validate Signatures is OFF, Keycloak will not verify signatures on the external ID Token, so alg/key-substitution tests are not meaningful.

For I1 key-rotation and trust-anchor tests against brokered OIDC identity providers, distinguish JWKS mode from static-key mode. With Use JWKS URL ON, Keycloak downloads and caches keys and refreshes on key changes; with it OFF, Keycloak uses the configured validating public key from its database and will not automatically pick up upstream key rotation.

For I1/I5 cross-provider JWT audience tests, ensure each identity provider has a unique issuer and each client has a unique subject identifier per issuer when using federated JWT client authentication such as Kubernetes or SPIFFE. Reusing issuer/subject combinations across providers invalidates the isolation oracle.

For I2 client-assertion replay tests, note the OIDC identity provider setting 'Allows client assertions to be re-used'. By default, a client assertion cannot be used multiple times; if this option is enabled, replay becomes by-design for that provider configuration and must not be flagged as a vulnerability.

For I1/I5 audience validation of client assertions, note the OIDC identity provider setting 'Allows Client ID as audience for assertions'. When enabled, the configured client ID is accepted as the audience instead of the token URL or issuer URL, which is explicitly non-standard. Tests must account for this alternate accepted audience to avoid false positives.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that restricts token-exchange or JWT-assertion scopes to those already present in the initial subject_token/assertion. Only downscoping is allowed when that executor is enforced. Tests must verify whether the downscope executor is configured before interpreting expanded scopes as a bug or absence of expansion as default behavior.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, do not assume the requesting frontend client is automatically present in the access token aud claim. Keycloak documentation states the frontend client itself is not automatically added as an audience; audience is typically added via audience mappers or audience resolve based on client roles.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests, client scopes with role scope mappings apply only if the user is permitted to use them. If there is no intersection between user roles and the client scope's role scope mappings, the scope's mappers and role mappings are omitted from the token. Missing claims or roles may therefore be by design.

For I5 role-grant tests, roles in issued tokens are the intersection of roles assigned to the user and role scope mappings of roles the client is permitted to access. Do not treat omission of user roles from the token as a bug unless the client's scope mappings should have allowed them.

For I4 username collision tests in identity brokering, account linking behavior depends on the configured First Login Flow. Default first-broker-login may create a new user, link an existing one after verification, or deny duplicates depending on authenticators such as Create User If Unique, Confirm Link Existing Account, Verify Existing Account By Email/Re-authentication, or Automatically Set Existing User.

For I4 case-confusion tests on brokered usernames, account for the identity-provider setting 'Case-sensitive username'. If disabled, the username from the identity provider is lower-cased when federating; apparent case-collisions may therefore be by design.

For I4 organization-group mapping tests, organization groups are isolated per organization and can share the same path across organizations. Group paths are relative to the organization, not globally unique. Do not treat same group path strings across organizations as identity or authorization collapse.

For I5 redirect-uri related tests on OIDC clients, Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default, with wildcard support only at the end of the pattern. If the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory traversal '/../', wildcard comparison is disabled and exact matching is used.

Client secret rotation uses a numeric sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Tests must not assume 0 disables rotation or preserves the old secret.
Password policy Hashing iterations uses a numeric sentinel: value -1 means use the default iteration count for the selected hashing algorithm, not literal negative iterations and not disable hashing.
Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses a numeric sentinel: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password, not 'no limit'.
User session limits use numeric sentinels: realm session limit 0 disables the check; client session limit 0 disables the check. Do not interpret 0 as zero allowed sessions.
WebAuthn timeout uses a numeric sentinel: value 0 means behavior depends on the authenticator implementation/default handling, not an immediate timeout.
CIBA policy has documented defaults: Expires In defaults to 120 seconds and Interval defaults to 5 seconds when not explicitly configured. Tests must not assume omitted values mean unlimited or zero.

Keycloak does not document a REST admin API in the provided docs for create_tenant, create_application, update_application, create_provider, configure_jwt_validation, create_user, update_user, delete_user, create_policy, create_identity_group, create_group_alias, seed_protected_resource, or cleanup_auth_method. The fuzzer must treat these operations as absent from this extraction and avoid inventing undocumented admin endpoints.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests against oidc_jwt client assertions, Keycloak documents that some JWT-based assertions can be re-used when the identity provider setting 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' is enabled. The fuzzer MUST treat repeated acceptance as by-configuration if this option is on, and MUST disable this option when testing anti-replay of client assertions.

For I1 issuer-validation tests on brokered OIDC identity providers, configure_jwt_validation MUST set the IdP 'Issuer' field. Keycloak validates issuer claims against this configured value; if it is omitted, the test cannot prove issuer enforcement.

For I1 signature-validation and key-rotation tests on brokered OIDC identity providers, 'Validate Signatures' MUST be ON. If it is OFF, Keycloak will not verify external ID Token signatures and alg/key-substitution tests are meaningless.

For I1 key-source and rotation tests, when 'Use JWKS URL' is ON Keycloak downloads and caches the external IdP public keys. The fuzzer MUST account for key caching when testing immediate trust-anchor rotation; a stale cached key can make a rotation test appear incoherent even though the system is operating by design.

For I1 kid-selection tests with static keys, if 'Validating Public Key Id' is not specified, Keycloak uses the configured validating public key for all requests regardless of the key ID sent by the external IDP. kid-based negative tests MUST set an explicit key id when testing key-id enforcement; otherwise kid mismatches are not meaningful.

For I2 authorization-code replay tests, Keycloak documents that the temporary code in Authorization Code Flow cannot be used more than once. The fuzzer MUST use the same code twice against the token endpoint and assert second use fails by status, not by identity comparison.

For I3 PKCE tests, the client's 'PKCE method' setting controls whether PKCE is required. Blank means PKCE is optional, not disabled. The fuzzer MUST configure S256 or plain when testing PKCE enforcement; otherwise exchange without code_verifier may succeed by design.

For I3 config-change tests involving default authentication behavior, Keycloak applies updated client and IdP configuration to new logins. A valid coherence test MUST compare behavior of the same request before and after the config change and must not flag expected behavior changes caused by legitimate admin updates.

For I3 browser-flow tests, Keycloak authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. Multi-step authorization-code and brokered-login sequences MUST complete before authentication session expiry or the client may receive an expired-authentication-session error unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I3 multi-tab or parallel browser tests, Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other tabs after one tab authenticates because of shared authentication session behavior. The fuzzer MUST isolate browser sessions when testing state/code swap or session binding, otherwise cross-tab auto-restart can mask the intended oracle.

For I4 username-collision tests in identity brokering, the general IdP setting 'Case-sensitive username' changes whether brokered usernames are preserved or lower-cased. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating. The fuzzer MUST treat case-folding collisions as by-configuration unless this option is enabled.

For I4 first-login linking tests, Keycloak's default first broker login flow may link or create users based on existing email/username and configured authenticators. The fuzzer MUST distinguish account-linking behavior from identity collapse bugs and should avoid auto-linking flows when testing principal binding unless the test explicitly targets linking.

For I4 dangerous auto-linking scenarios, the 'Automatically Set Existing User' first-login authenticator is explicitly documented as dangerous and links without verification. If such a flow is configured, identity merges are by design. The fuzzer MUST not report principal-binding violations caused solely by this authenticator.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, Keycloak documents that the frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. The fuzzer MUST not assume client_id appears in aud unless an Audience or Audience Resolve mapper adds it.

For I5 audience-mismatch and cross-provider audience tests, Keycloak requires explicit audience configuration through Audience or Audience Resolve mappers and recommends services verify aud themselves. The fuzzer MUST create the necessary audience mapping before expecting aud enforcement outcomes.

For I5 scope-escalation tests in token exchange and JWT authorization grant, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that restricts requested scopes to those already present in the initial subject_token or assertion. If this executor is not enforced, broader scopes may be granted according to normal client configuration. The fuzzer MUST enable the downscope assertion grant enforcer before treating expanded scopes as a violation.

For I5 client-scope permission tests, a client scope with role scope mappings only applies if the user is permitted to use it, meaning there must be an intersection between user roles and client-scope roles. Missing claims or scopes can be caused by scope-permission filtering rather than authorization bugs.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses value -1 as a sentinel meaning use the default iteration count for the selected hashing algorithm, not literal negative one and not disable hashing. Never assume -1 disables the underlying check.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses value 0 to mean the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password. Value 0 is strict immediate re-authentication, not 'use default' and not 'disable'.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn policy 'Timeout' uses value 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator implementation. Value 0 is not guaranteed to mean immediate expiry and not guaranteed to disable the operation.
Numeric sentinel: User session limits use value 0 to disable the session-count check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Value 0 means disabled, not literal zero allowed sessions.

Numeric sentinel: Client secret rotation 'Rotated Secret Expiration' uses value 0 to mean the old secret is immediately removed during rotation. Value 0 is immediate invalidation, not default retention.

Numeric sentinel: OIDC identity provider 'Client Assertion Signature Algorithm' defaults when unspecified: RS256 for private-key JWT and HS256 for client-secret JWT. Omitting the algorithm does not disable assertion signing; it selects a non-empty default.
Numeric sentinel: OIDC identity provider 'Client Assertion Audience' defaults to the IdP token endpoint URL when unspecified. Omitting it does not mean no audience binding.

Numeric sentinel: CIBA policy 'Expires In' defaults to 120 seconds and 'Interval' defaults to 5 seconds when not set. Tests relying on auth_req_id lifetime or polling cadence MUST not assume unset means unlimited or zero.

Session-use budget: Keycloak user session limits count concurrent sessions, not per-token API-call uses. However, if the realm/client is configured with session-count limiting in authentication flows, additional logins created by verification or parallel test setup can trigger denial or oldest-session termination. The fuzzer MUST avoid creating extra sessions during a single sequence when session-count limits are low.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the URL pattern, and wildcard comparison is disabled when the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory path traversal. For redirect_uri_mismatch and code-injection tests, the fuzzer MUST use an exactly registered redirect_uri unless it is explicitly testing wildcard behavior.

For PKCE tests, client setting PKCE method has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is optional and not enforced; S256 means PKCE is required with S256; plain means PKCE is required with plain. Do NOT interpret blank as 'disabled endpoint' or as enforcement. To test pkce_skip or pkce_not_required_public_client, configure the client with PKCE method=S256 or plain; otherwise omission of code_verifier is by design.

Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived by design. For I2 replay tests on authorization code flow, reuse of the same code should fail, but this is about code replay, not JWT replay. Do not generalize this behavior to stateless JWT bearer tokens.

For OIDC broker issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST set issuer explicitly. Documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims against the configured Issuer value. If Issuer is omitted, the test cannot prove issuer enforcement.

For OIDC broker signature-validation tests (alg_none, resign_attacker_key, trust_anchor_substitution, kid_injection), configure_jwt_validation MUST enable validate_signatures and provide trust material via jwks_url or validating_public_key. If Validate Signatures is OFF, acceptance of unsigned or attacker-signed ID tokens is expected configuration, not a vulnerability.

When Use JWKS URL is OFF and Validating Public Key Id is empty, Keycloak uses the validating public key for all requests regardless of the key ID sent by the external IDP. Therefore kid-based negative tests are not meaningful in this mode. To test kid handling, either use JWKS URL mode or set an explicit validating public key id.

Keycloak caches public keys of external OIDC identity providers for performance. For jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, a valid test must account for documented key caching and verify rejection only after the broker has refreshed trust material according to the configured JWKS/static-key mode.

For oidc_sso_audience_cross_tenant and cross_provider_jwt_audience tests, each brokered OIDC identity provider/client pairing must use a distinct configured Client ID and Issuer. The fuzzer MUST present an ID token whose aud does not match the target provider's configured client_id and assert rejection. Reusing the same client_id across providers invalidates the oracle.

OIDC broker login is authorization-code based. After the external IdP authenticates the user, Keycloak fetches user profile information from UserInfo using the access token. Therefore tests that expect identity mapping from ID token alone may be misinterpreted; user profile claims can come from UserInfo and configured claim names.

Identity provider general configuration 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression format. For multi-identity I4 tests, do not assume exact-only matching for this field. If the fuzzer needs multiple identities to pass the same broker constraint, it may use a regex that matches all intended values; using '*' semantics depends on regex, not glob.

Case-sensitive username has by-design identity semantics: when disabled, the username from the identity provider is lower-cased when federating users; when enabled, the original username is kept for the federated identity, but server usernames are always lower-case. For case_confusion I4 tests, configure this setting deliberately and do not treat lowercasing as an unexpected collision without accounting for this documented behavior.

First broker login can create a new local account or link to an existing one based on email/username and configured authenticators. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control the First Login Flow. Automatic linking or Automatically Set Existing User can intentionally merge identities and would otherwise look like a collision bug.

The AutoLink authenticator is explicitly documented as dangerous and automatically links existing accounts without prompting. If a test realm uses such a first login flow, identity merges are by design. Do not flag them as I4 unless the flow was configured to require stronger verification.

For jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth-style coherence tests on broker config, NEW logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated configuration. A valid I3 test must show whether the same brokered token/request is evaluated inconsistently across a config change boundary, not merely that admin changes altered future behavior.

Client scopes linked as Optional are only applied when requested via the scope parameter in the authorization request. For I5 audience and scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST request the relevant optional scopes explicitly; absence of claims or audiences without the scope request is by design.

Client scopes permissions are intersection-based: if a client scope has role scope mappings, the user must be a member of at least one of those roles or the scope is not applied and will not appear in the token. For I5 tests, missing claims from a requested scope may be due to scope permission filtering rather than a token issuance bug.

Access token roles are the intersection of roles assigned to the user and role scope mappings of roles the client is permitted to access. For group_policy_escalation and identity_policy_override tests, the oracle must compare against this documented intersection, not against all user roles or all group roles.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. If the fuzzer expects aud to contain the requesting client_id by default, that expectation is wrong. Use hardcoded audience or audience resolve configuration when testing audience binding.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Keycloak documents a client policy executor that can enforce downscoping so exchanged scopes are restricted to those present in the initial subject_token/assertion. The fuzzer MUST record whether such a client policy is configured; otherwise broader exchanged scopes may reflect policy absence rather than a bypass.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the token endpoint with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and set audience explicitly. Also note that audience simulation outside token exchange is not generally applicable; docs state audience parameter is currently supported for token exchange.

For OIDC logout tests, if post_logout_redirect_uri is included then either client_id or id_token_hint must also be included, and post_logout_redirect_uri must match one of the client's Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs. Missing redirect after logout without these prerequisites is by design.

Client secret rotation has numeric sentinel semantics: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Do not assume overlap exists when value is 0. Secret rotation also does not happen automatically; it occurs on client update or regenerate-secret actions.

Password policy Hashing iterations has numeric sentinel semantics: value -1 means use the default iteration count for the selected hashing algorithm, not literal negative or disabled hashing. Never assume -1 disables verification.
Maximum Authentication Age password policy has numeric sentinel semantics: value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password. It does not mean 'no limit'.

WebAuthn timeout has numeric sentinel semantics: value 0 means behavior depends on the authenticator implementation, not strict zero timeout and not disabled WebAuthn. Do not use 0 as a deterministic expiry oracle.
User session count limiter has numeric sentinel semantics: realm max sessions or client max sessions value 0 disables that check. It does not mean zero sessions allowed.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. Multi-tab/browser-flow stress tests must account for eviction of old sub-sessions rather than treating it as random state confusion.

Authentication sessions usually expire after 30 minutes by default via Login timeout. Multi-step browser/OIDC tests that pause too long may fail due to expired authentication session and automatic restart behavior across tabs; this is not necessarily an I3 flaw.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
